summary: A satirical, humorous feature dated October 15, 2023 that walks through the stages of college athletic recruitment, from first mailbox contact through unofficial and official visits, in-home visits, scholarships, verbal commitments, Signing Day, and walk-ons. Each stage is illustrated with quotes from nicknamed young athletes. It concludes that the process is a mix of hope, hype and hyperbole, but that youthful dreams and scholarships are real.
one_line: A satirical October 2023 tour of the college athletic recruitment process, from recruitment letters to Signing Day, told through quirky young athletes.
key_facts: The article is dated October 15, 2023 and is filed under the topic 'Local Sports and Activities'.
Since September, athletes like 17-year-old track phenom Sarah "Sprint" Simmons and Tommy "Touchdown" Tucker have received piles of university pamphlets and coach letters.
Tommy Tucker's family received so many recruitment letters that they began mistaking the mailman for Santa Claus.
Jenny "Juke" Jones, a soccer player from Oaktree High, took so many unofficial visits that she accumulated frequent flyer miles for a round trip to Mars; she wore cleats on the plane.
Official visits begin in September; athletes get facility tours and swag and are 'dined' (legally speaking).
Johnny "Jumper" Reynolds, a basketball player, joked that his love language is 'all-you-can-eat pasta' during an official visit.
During an in-home visit, a coach used Billy "Base" Roberts's mom's irreplaceable vase as a prop to demonstrate a swing.
An anonymous valedictorian with a 4.5 GPA who runs the 100-meter dash quickly joked about choosing universities by sprinting and high-jumping, asking who needs AP Calculus.
A verbal commitment is non-binding; the National Letter of Intent (NLI) is likened to a prenup.
Wide receiver "Swifty" Pete Peterson gave verbal commitments to five different colleges during September to keep his options open.
Volleyball star Samantha "Slam" Sanchez said she practiced her signature more than her serve before Signing Day.
Walk-ons are compared to Rudy Ruettiger and earn team spots without a scholarship; Chad "Chase" Chaserton delivers inspirational monologues ('I've got heart pumping out of my shinguards!').
